answer.rationale: Memory 44 directly indicates stronger pipeline quality for sales-assisted enterprise conversion, a meaningful proxy for qualified revenue, but omits retention, deal economics, and realized long-term revenue. Memory 57 is comparatively strong because it explicitly reports qualified revenue and no measurable retention harm, though it omits longer-horizon retention, incentive cost, and scalability. Memories 31 and 86 show activation, completion, and time-to-value improvements—important leading indicators—but do not establish qualified revenue, monetization, or retention. Memory 73 reports acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMBs, but does not address discount durability, margin, retention, or adverse selection under competitive pricing. Memory 91 only establishes improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action; it provides the weakest direct evidence for sustainable long-term qualified revenue.
